turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: What does this matter of tenantry and territory have to do with the Mussulmans' threats?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Do not lecture me, Nikhil, on what is right and what is wrong. If you want to keep your followers from fleeing to my estates, perhaps you should treat them better.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You're so quick to defend your people, Nikhil, but do you even know what's at stake here? I'd rather take a chance with the Mussulmans than live in fear of my own shadows.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, you're not seriously expecting me to be cowed by a few empty threats, are you? I've faced worse odds and come out on top, with my estate intact and my people thriving.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your words, Sandip. My duty is to protect my people, and I will not compromise that duty for the sake of your estate or your pride.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I think we're forgetting one thing, Nikhil: what about the Mussulmans' grievances? Have you considered why they're making these threats in the first place?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I suggest you focus on your own estate, Sandip, rather than lecturing me on how to manage mine. As for the Mussulmans' grievances, I am well aware of them, and that is precisely why I am warning you to take precautions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I see, Nikhil, you're not just a one-trick pony with a taste for the dramatic, you're also a master of understatement. My estate's been thriving for generations, and a few empty threats aren't going to change that.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your flippant attitude, Sandip. This is not a matter for jest or bravado, but a serious warning that requires attention and action.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I suggest you take this warning seriously, Sandip, and do not dismiss it as mere posturing. The safety of our people is at stake, and I will not stand idly by while you gamble with their lives.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, perhaps we could discuss the Mussulmans' grievances further, in private, if you'd like.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I've noticed that the Mussulmans have been increasingly restless, and I've heard whispers of their discontent. Perhaps it's worth exploring the root causes of their grievances.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, your words are laced with a certain... detachment, but do you truly believe the Mussulmans' discontent will simply fade away?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the theatrics, Nikhil. I'm not some naive simpleton who'll fall for your dire warnings without a fight. I've got my own ways of handling these Mussulmans, and they don't involve cowering in fear like a coward.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps it would be wise to consider the long-term consequences of your actions, rather than simply reacting to the immediate situation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I've got a better idea, Nikhil. Why don't you and your ilk worry about your own crumbling estates, and I'll take care of the Mussulmans with my own brand of zamindari charm?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, the Mussulmans will not be swayed by your 'zamindari charm'. Their grievances run deep, and I fear your actions will only exacerbate the situation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I'm shaking in my boots, Nikhil. You and your prophecies of doom are as predictable as they are tedious. I'll take my chances with the Mussulmans, and I'm sure my charm will only make them love me more.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What's the matter, Nikhil? Did your fortune teller also predict that I'd be the one to bring about the downfall of our esteemed community?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in this futile banter with you, Sandip. The well-being of our community is at stake, and I will not stand idly by while you recklessly court disaster.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
